newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on Brazil bond success.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on Brazil bond success.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished much higher Thursday, boosted by Brazil's markets after the launch of its $3.0 billion 30-year global bond and debt buyback.

"The market was given the impulse by Brazils' buyback. It was pretty successful," said a trader at a foreign bank, adding that price gains in the Brazilian bond Thursday added to the firmness of the markets in the region.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 3/8 at 93-6/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.15 at 123.70.
Another trader said Argentine bonds were also gaining because "some hope they will do the same (a debt buyback) here."
The trader said there was buyer interest both from abroad and locally Thursday.

Still, players cautioned the market was eagerly awaiting the release of U.S. jobless figures Friday, which could be trend-setting for the coming weeks as it could give clues on the likely course of U.S. monetary policy.
Traders said activity picked up this session, with busier trade in most instruments.
Call money rates fell to 5.63 percent from 5.78 percent.
